title: A steady monthly poverty rate can hide long and unequal poverty spells
source_unit: U.S. Census Bureau Current Population Reports P70BR-216, using the 2025 Survey of Income and Program Participation for the 2024 reference year
geography: United States; nationally representative SIPP population and reported age, race/Hispanic-origin, sex, and educational-attainment groups

denominator.unit: SIPP people in the relevant monthly or episodic poverty universe

monthly_poverty_rate.value: 11.9% in January; no significant month-to-month change through 2024
monthly_poverty_rate.unit: share of people in monthly official poverty

episodic_poverty_rate.unit: share of people in poverty for at least two consecutive months

full_year_share_among_episodic.unit: share of people who experienced episodic poverty and were poor all 12 months

child_episodic_rate.unit: share of children under 18 experiencing episodic poverty

older_adult_duration.value: approximately 11 months mean duration; 79.4% poor all 12 months among older adults experiencing episodic poverty
older_adult_duration.unit: poverty duration among people age 65 and over experiencing episodic poverty

race_episodic_rates.value: 20.8% non-Hispanic Black; 21.3% Hispanic; 11.6% non-Hispanic White; 12.7% non-Hispanic Asian
race_episodic_rates.unit: share of each reported race/Hispanic-origin group experiencing episodic poverty

downstream_outcomes.unit: assistance receipt, housing, food hardship, health, work, care, trust, and later recovery linked to a poverty spell

observations.method: Official Census brief using monthly family income-to-poverty ratios and the official pre-tax money-income poverty measure; episodic poverty is defined as poverty for at least two consecutive months, with the episodic universe limited to people observed in the poverty universe for all 12 months.
observations.uncertainty: The source reports estimates and 90% confidence margins of error, but the public brief does not provide a retained person-level extract for this record. Poverty status uses pre-tax money income, family composition, and monthly CPI-U-adjusted thresholds that do not vary geographically. The estimates do not identify the event that caused a spell or the resources that buffered it.
observations.subgroup: Children, adults 18-64, adults 65 and over, men, women, mutually exclusive non-Hispanic White, non-Hispanic Black, non-Hispanic Asian, Hispanic, and educational-attainment groups.
observations.counterinterpretation: A long official-poverty spell is not identical to constant material deprivation: assets, informal support, noncash benefits, consumption, debt, housing costs, geography, and measurement timing may differ. Group differences describe exposure and duration, not a single causal mechanism.

related_sources.claim: Census publication page identifies the brief, author, date, and SIPP basis.
Census documents the 2025 SIPP primary file, replicate weights, longitudinal weights, and data-quality caution.

boundary: This record adds a measured distinction between a monthly poverty rate and the duration and concentration of poverty spells. It does not establish causes, assistance take-up, material hardship, household coping, trust, political action, or later recovery for the same people.
